name: shiftwork_clock_out
title: Shift work: clock out
description: Shift-work clock-out: record that a unit finished — set its status, advance plan.cursor, merge `handoff_patch` into handoff, push `history_entry` onto the 5-entry history ring, and append one accounting line to <checkpoint>.log.jsonl. Call it once per unit after its agent returns: shiftwork_clock_in briefs, this tool closes, and shiftwork_status reads what both wrote. The whole mutated document is validated against the checkpoint schema BEFORE one atomic write, so a failure writes nothing and answers {"result": "error", "reason": ...}; nothing is ever deleted from the checkpoint. `unit_id` must be plan.cursor — which needs no brief and clocks out with briefed=false — or a unit clock_in briefed since its own last clock-out; any other id is refused with `unit X is not the cursor unit Y`. `handoff_patch` and `history_entry` are both required arguments: pass `{}` to leave handoff unchanged, and give history_entry at least `unit` and `outcome`. plan.cursor then moves to the head of the ready batch recomputed on the new document — plan.units order over the remaining non-terminal units when the graph cannot batch, `unit_id` when none remain. The accounting line carries unit, role, status, ts and `briefed` (written by the runtime, never taken from you: true only when a brief was issued since this unit's LAST clock-out) plus your `accounting` fields when given. When job.roles names this unit's role, `accounting.model` must be on that role's list, spelled exactly, or nothing is written — see the `model` property.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
checkpoint.description: Path to the shift-work checkpoint JSON file (by convention .shiftwork/checkpoint.json in the repo the job works on), absolute or relative to the server's working directory. The same file shiftwork_plan, shiftwork_clock_in and shiftwork_clock_out take; it must validate against assets/schemas/shiftwork-checkpoint.json.

unit_id.title: Unit Id
unit_id.description: The unit being clocked out. Must be plan.cursor, or a unit briefed since its own last clock-out: clock_in briefs the cursor unit by default and, when its unit_id names one, any unit shiftwork_plan reports in `ready` — and that brief is what lets clock_out accept a unit the cursor is not on.

status.title: Status
status.description: The unit's new status; the same five values the checkpoint schema allows on plan.units[].status.

handoff_patch.title: Handoff Patch
handoff_patch.description: Shallow-merged into `handoff`: only these four keys exist there, and a key outside them is refused by the schema check. Required; `{}` leaves `handoff` unchanged.

open_questions.description: The autonomy switch: empty = driver keeps cycling, non-empty = STOP and ask.

do_not.description: Negative space — near-mistakes past sessions made.

notes.description: Free-form prose for the next session, one string; the empty string clears it.

history_entry.title: History Entry
history_entry.description: Pushed onto the 5-entry `history` ring; `unit` and `outcome` are required, `notes` optional, other keys pass through.

unit.description: The unit this entry is about — normally the `unit_id` being clocked out.

outcome.description: What happened, in a few words: done, blocked on X, dropped because Y.

notes.description: Optional free text for the next session reading the ring.

anyOf.description: Per-unit cost. Written verbatim, beside ts/unit/role/status, as one line of <checkpoint>.log.jsonl - the ledger the N-sessions experiment reads. The keys named here have fixed meanings so a reader holding only the ledger knows what each number counts, in which unit, and which model produced it; any other key passes through unchanged, except the five the runtime writes itself — unit, role, status, ts, event — which are refused (result=error) before anything is written; a self-reported briefed is overwritten, not refused. Lines written before this schema existed may spell these differently; the schema governs new writes only.

tokens.description: Tokens the unit consumed as the harness's subagent counter reports them: every class it reports (input, output, cache creation) summed, EXCLUDING cache reads. In a non-null accounting line it is required — a line without it is refused before anything is written; only `accounting: null`, the default, is exempt, and that logs no cost at all. A rounded self-estimate is allowed only if `note` says it is one; a unit whose cost is unknown cannot be compared with any other.

cache_read_tokens.description: Tokens the unit's requests served from prompt cache, kept OUT of `tokens` because they dominate a real session's traffic and would swamp the work signal. Optional: omit it when the harness reports no such figure - a written 0 means the unit read nothing from cache.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock from spawning the subagent to its final message, in whole milliseconds. In a non-null line it is required, and it is the only duration key with a defined meaning: older lines carry `duration`, `duration_min` or `duration_s`, which this schema neither reads nor renames.

model.description: The exact identifier of the model the subagent actually ran on (e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`) and nothing else - a caveat about how it was chosen belongs in `note`. Not required here: when the checkpoint's job.roles names this unit's role, clock_out already requires it and refuses a value off that role's list, spelled exactly; a checkpoint with no job.roles leaves it optional. This schema does not change that gate.

tool_uses.description: Tool calls the subagent made, as the harness counts them. Optional; it is the denominator that makes `tokens` comparable across units of different size (per-unit cost is linear in tool calls, not in unit length).

note.description: Free text for what the fields above cannot say: that `tokens` is an estimate, that this is a retry or a second scope under the same unit id, what a harness counter excludes. Anything that is not a model identifier goes here, not in `model`.

accounting.title: Accounting
accounting.description: Per-unit cost line, or null (the default) to log a line with no cost figures at all. A non-null line must carry `tokens` and `duration_ms`; `model` is required when job.roles names this unit's role. The object shape is described below.

result.description: `ok` when the checkpoint was rewritten; `error` with `reason` when the call was refused and nothing was written.

log.description: Path of the <checkpoint>.log.jsonl the accounting line was appended to.

reason.description: With result `error`: one sentence saying why the call was refused.
